lines.text: Not everything. But enough to stop pretending you don't.
Someone once wanted a world with nothing bad in it. It's a kind wish. Most terrible things begin as kind wishes.
Every sad day, every cruel word, every fear... they cut it out, and put it where nobody would have to look.
It didn't vanish. Nothing ever does. It only piled up in the dark, and waited.
What you fought down here wasn't a monster. It was everything nobody wanted to feel.
And you won. Of course you won. It's very tired.
But beating it doesn't send it anywhere. There is nowhere left to send it.
That's the hard thing about understanding. It doesn't fix anything. It only takes away the excuse.
Some people learn the truth and think the work is over. That's usually where it starts.
The things we hide from ourselves don't disappear. They grow quiet, and heavy, and patient.
You can't throw away the bad parts of a life. You can only learn to carry them. A little at a time.
Somewhere up there, a voice is still repeating the same words, hoping someone will listen to the end.
A light that went out one night is still waiting for someone to ask why.
And a few old words were never read to the one they were written for.
Unfinished things are like that. They don't call your name. They just wait by the door.
Rest, if you can. The quiet up there will hold. For now.
And when you're ready... come back down. It will still be here, waiting to be finished.
